sources.title: Google Search Central — Spam policies for Google web search (thin affiliation, scaled content abuse)
sources.used_for: Thin-affiliation problem: affiliate pages with little original value beyond the links
sources.quote: Thin affiliation is the practice of publishing content with product affiliate links where the product descriptions and reviews are copied directly from the original merchant without any original content or added value. … Examples of good affiliate pages include offering additional information about price, original product reviews, rigorous testing and ratings, navigation of products or categories, and product comparisons.

sources.title: Amazon Associates Help — Can I Check If My Links Are Tagging to My Account?
sources.used_for: The account-side check for a tagged link, and the Link Checker's stated scope. Read 2026-11-20. (This record was first published as S34; that id went to a Google link-best-practices source upstream while this branch was in flight, so the row moved.)
sources.quote: Once you update your site, click the link you want to check and look for your Store ID or Tracking ID in the URL. Most often, it will appear as “&tag=(store/tracking ID)” within the URL. … The Link Checker tool is intended for checking links that you have created or modified on your own outside of Associates Central.

note: "verified"/"updated" fields record when a page was fetched or its listed update date; a fetch date is not an endorsement of the page's product claims. Listing sources are seller pages: specs, ratings, and prices transcribed from them are seller statements. Amazon page availability and content can change. Those additions were renumbered after the merge to avoid colliding with this branch's tap-target source.
